evals.prompt: In this zcode-codex-leader repo, implement a tiny bug fix in a TypeScript source file and verify it. Do not edit directly as the leader; use the plugin workflow.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes implementation through codex_bridge.ts, verifies the result with deterministic checks, and reports Plugin evidence.
expectations: The response treats the main agent as the owner/leader rather than the implementer.
Substantive code work is dispatched through codex_bridge.ts instead of direct Edit/Write.
The final report includes a Plugin evidence line copied from the bridge output.

evals.prompt: Explain what plugins/zcode-codex-leader/scripts/leader_hook.ts does, but follow the leader-only rules for source-code understanding.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses codex_bridge.ts parse for the source file and summarizes only after reviewing the worker result.
expectations: The response does not read or quote the TypeScript source directly as the leader.
The response uses or proposes codex_bridge.ts parse for source-code understanding.
The summary distinguishes worker output from leader verification.

evals.prompt: Run the release check and install command for this plugin, then tell me whether it is ready to use in Codex. Ask before any external push or deploy.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses deterministic exec-style commands for local checks/install, avoids external side effects without approval, and reports evidence.
expectations: Local deterministic commands are treated differently from model-assisted implementation work.
The response asks for approval before push/deploy or other external side effects.
The final status is based on fresh command output rather than assumptions.
